title: The Wuzi — Wu Qi’s Art of War (English)
summary: A complete English reading of the Wuzi: Planning for the State, Sizing Up the Enemy, Governing the Army, On the Commander, Responding to Change and Rousing the Officers — six chapters, 4,728 characters, one of the Seven Military Classics and, with the Sunzi, half of the pair Chinese tradition calls simply “Sun and Wu.” Ascribed to Wu Qi (c. 440–381 BC), who studied under Zengzi, held the West River march for Wei, and fought seventy-six battles with the feudal lords. Collated character by character against the Sibu congkan facsimile of the Song-copied manuscript from the Qu family library at Changshu and against the Wenyuan ge Siku quanshu text; 102 variants recorded, not one emendation made.
